_comment: M14.0.SPEC (#290) — markdown completeness classification. Every public NAMED node type of BOTH pinned wasms is in exactly one bucket: 51 distinct from wasm/tree-sitter-markdown.wasm (the block grammar, 207 nodeTypeForId slots) and 26 from wasm/tree-sitter-markdown_inline.wasm (the companion inline grammar, 153 slots), for a UNION of 70 distinct names after the 7 the two share. Silence is guilt: a type in no bucket fails section A, and a type neither grammar produces any more is a stale row and also fails. The handled set was derived MECHANICALLY, not by eye — every double-quoted literal in src/ast/real-markdown-analyzer.ts was intersected with the two grammars' named-type sets (29 of 70), and the 41 un-named types are each classified below with a measured site count over the lane's pinned corpus (scala3@18df09c0, 738 tracked .md files). 29 handled_verified + 39 internal_silent + 2 gap = 70.

handled_verified.note: Twenty-nine types, every one pinned. The six `atx_hN_marker` and two `setext_hN_underline` types are how a heading's LEVEL is read — from the marker's own name, never from the marker's text, so a document that indents its heading markers differently still nests correctly. `atx_heading`/`setext_heading` are the two containers and they are handled TOGETHER because their text lives in different places: an ATX heading's text is its `inline` child, a setext heading's is the first line of its paragraph, and the analyzer branches on the container type rather than falling through from one to the other. That branch is not cosmetic — see the MD-D7 entry in the design decisions, where the wrong branch published a heading name containing a newline. `fenced_code_block` + `info_string` + `language` are the code-fence triple: the block is the site, the info string names the language, and the `language` child is preferred over the info string's own text because a fence can carry a title after the language. `pipe_table` + `pipe_table_header` + `pipe_table_cell` are the table triple, and the pair `minus_metadata` / `plus_metadata` is deliberately NOT a triple — see the plus_metadata gap entry. `link_destination` is read in BOTH grammars' shapes (an inline link's own child, and a reference definition's destination) and `link_label` carries the reference in the full form while `link_text` carries it in the collapsed and shortcut forms, so the three reference-link types plus those two are one contract, not five. `image` is read only for its REFERENCE form; an inline-form image's destination is its `link_destination` child and is already handled. `document` is the walk root.

internal_silent.note: Thirty-nine types that correctly emit nothing, each with a measured reason rather than a shrug. INLINE PRESENTATION (17 types): `emphasis`/`emphasis_delimiter`/`strong_emphasis`/`strikethrough`/`code_span`/`code_span_delimiter`/`hard_line_break`/`latex_block`/`latex_span_delimiter`/`backslash_escape`/`entity_reference`/`numeric_character_reference`/`link_text`'s siblings — formatting is not a graph fact. The load-bearing member of this group is `code_span`: a link inside one is excluded STRUCTURALLY, because the inline grammar gives a code span only ANONYMOUS children and the walker descends NAMED children only, so no `link_destination` is reachable beneath it. That is a property a reader can check, and it is what F9-PROBE-MD6 pins — if a future grammar gave `code_span` a named destination child, the probe fails and the exclusion has to become an explicit guard. A link inside `strong_emphasis` IS published, because those are named nodes with named children, and that is also correct. `latex_block` and `latex_span_delimiter` are the math forms; they carry no destination and no identity. LIST STRUCTURE (9 types, measured 6,264 `list_item` sites over 372 files): a list is a container, its items are containers, and its markers are presentation. What the lane DOES publish from inside a list is every link in its inline content, which the M12 contract probe pins ('link inside list item uses edge'). TASK MARKERS (2 types, 17 checked sites in 1 file): a checkbox is state, not a name; the doc declares them as noise. BLOCK CONTAINERS (6 types): `paragraph` and `section` are the grammar's structural wrappers — `section` in particular is a pure nesting artifact with no content of its own; `block_quote`/`block_quote_marker`/`block_continuation` likewise, and the links inside a quote ARE published (contract probe: 'link inside blockquote uses edge', 49 quote sites over 25 files). `thematic_break` (212 sites over 200 files) is `---`/`***`/___ and is worth naming for a specific reason: it is visually identical to a setext H2 underline, so a reader who assumed the marker was a break would mis-describe every setext heading in the lane. FENCE FURNITURE (2 types, 4,076 `code_fence_content` sites over 607 files): the fence's body text and its ``` delimiters are not facts; the language and the site are. TABLE FURNITURE (5 types, 224 `pipe_table_row` sites over 14 files): the analyzer reads the table's HEADER row and stops. A body cell is DATA — the same ruling toml's spec records for a value, and it is why a 224-row corpus of table bodies produces no symbols and no edges. RAW HTML (2 types, 579 `html_block` sites over 291 files — the largest silent class in the lane): the block grammar models a raw HTML block as an opaque region, and the companion inline grammar's `html_tag` covers inline raw HTML. Neither is a link destination. The corpus-errors artifact already names the one place this costs real recovery (`<details>` indented inside a numbered-list item, an ERROR at each list-item boundary), and that is a GRAMMAR limitation recorded against the grammar, not an analyzer gap. ZERO-SITE TYPES, named so the count is on the record rather than implied: `entity_reference` and `numeric_character_reference` are 0 over 738 files, which is why the character-reference ruling below is declared rather than measured. ERROR AND MISSING ARE THE ENGINE'S, NOT THE ANALYZER'S, and that boundary is the whole reason they are here rather than in handled_verified: `engine.ts` walks the parsed tree and pushes a `ParseError` for every `node.type === "ERROR" || node.isMissing` (the one condition, the one diagnostic, anchored to the offending node's own 1-based span), while `real-markdown-analyzer.ts` names NEITHER literal — measured, 0 occurrences in its source. So a markdown parse error is reported by the shared engine path every language uses, and the lane's own error contract is the four NAMED grammar limits in markdown-corpus-errors.json, not a recovery walk: 12 error nodes over 4 of 738 corpus files, all four named, 0 unexpected, 0 crashes. This is the same split the html spec records for the same two types, reached independently on a second grammar — ERROR reported, MISSING silent — and the useful part is that two lanes agree on it by measurement rather than by copying.

gaps.measured: 2 sites in 2 of 738 corpus files. Small, but it is an ASYMMETRY inside one construct rather than a missing feature: a FENCED code block publishes `code_block.<lang>` as a per-site `function` symbol, and an INDENTED one publishes nothing at all. A reader of the graph cannot tell 'this document has no code' from 'this document has code the lane dropped'.
gaps.why_open: Left open rather than classified silent on purpose. `internal_silent` means 'correctly emits nothing', and for a code block the correct answer is a symbol — the fenced form proves the lane has one. Classifying it silent would make the count zero and the question closed, which is the 'silent gap' the M14 standing rules call the actual shame.
gaps.fix: One more branch on the block DFS emitting `code_block` (no language) per site, sharing the fenced path's site identity so an indented and a fenced block under one heading do not collide. Pinned by a fixture and a probe, and the two corpus files are named so the fix can be measured rather than argued.
gaps.missing: an INDENTED code block (4-space) publishes nothing, while a FENCED one publishes `code_block.<lang>` as a per-site `function`. 2 sites in 2 of 738 corpus files. The count is small; the ASYMMETRY inside one construct is not, and a reader of the graph cannot distinguish 'this document has no code' from 'this document has code the lane dropped'. Fix is one more branch on the block DFS sharing the fenced path's site identity, pinned by a fixture and a probe with the two corpus files named so the fix is measured rather than argued.

gaps.measured: 0 sites in 738 corpus files. The construct is Pandoc/MyST title-block front matter (`+++` fences) against the lane's `---` reading.
gaps.why_open: The count is 0, so this lane can neither support nor refute a claim about it, and a fixture for a dialect with no corpus would be a pin with nothing behind it — the same reasoning the css lane records for `.sass`/`.less`. It is filed as a gap rather than a declared boundary because it is the same construct the lane already handles in its other spelling, so the asymmetry is real even where the corpus is silent.
gaps.fix: One more node type on the front-matter branch, with the `+++` form decided by measurement against a real MyST corpus when one is pinned. NOT to be implemented against an invented fixture.
gaps.missing: Pandoc/MyST `+++` title-block front matter publishes nothing against the lane's `---` reading. 0 sites in 738 corpus files, so this lane can neither support nor refute a claim about it and a fixture for a dialect with no corpus would be a pin with nothing behind it (the css lane's `.sass`/`.less` precedent). Filed because it is the same construct already handled in its other spelling, so the asymmetry is real even where the corpus is silent. NOT to be implemented against an invented fixture; owed a real MyST corpus.

decisions.question: Should a reference link with NO matching `link_reference_definition` publish a `uses` edge to its bare label? RULED: no. CommonMark is explicit — 'If a link reference definition has not been defined for the link label, then it is not a link', and the construct renders as literal text.
decisions.measured: The alternative was implemented and MEASURED before being rejected: publishing the undefined case produced 171 edges across 34 of 738 corpus files, and sampling them showed the class dominated by bare bracketed citation markers (`NOTICE.md: document -> 1`, six times in one file). Those are fabricated endpoints and an R10 target-spelling violation, because `1` is not a name this lane spells its symbols with.
decisions.consequence: An undefined reference is INVISIBLE rather than flagged, so a reader cannot distinguish 'this document has a broken reference' from 'this document never had one'. That is a real limitation and it is a decision. The two rejected alternatives were publishing 171 fabrications, or inventing a suppression heuristic — and a heuristic with no evidence behind it is what this repository refuses most loudly.
decisions.pinned_by: F9-PROBE-MD1b, whose FORBID half also asserts the ORACLE refuses it, so the day the oracle starts deriving it the probe fails as COLLUSION rather than the lane quietly agreeing with itself.

decisions.question: Is a heading's published NAME its source text or its rendered text? RULED: its source text, with exactly two corrections that are grammar facts rather than style — the ATX closing run is removed, and an empty heading publishes ABSENCE.
decisions.measured: The rendered-text alternative has NO corpus evidence: `entity_reference` and `numeric_character_reference` are 0 over 738 files, and a 99-line fixture corpus is not a basis for a contract. So the source-text spelling stands, the two corrections stand on the pinned grammar's own shape, and the wider question is recorded here as UNDECIDED rather than answered by assertion.
decisions.consequence: Two headings that RENDER identically but differ in markup publish two symbols (`## **Setup**` and `## Setup`), and a formatting-only edit changes a symbol's identity. Stated rather than hidden. The corrections are load-bearing on their own: without the closing-run removal a document that closes its headings and one that does not produce two symbols for the same section, and without the absence rule a document of empty headings publishes a `contains` chain named `#` -> `##` -> `###`, which is the M60 R7 class (a name that is not a name).
decisions.pinned_by: markdown/heading-identity, whose `forbidSymbols` half carries the absent-name contract, and F9-PROBE-MD10 for the closing run.

decisions.question: Should a table's BODY rows publish symbols or `contains` edges? RULED: no. A header cell is a column NAME — the identity of the table's structure — and a body cell is DATA.
decisions.measured: 224 `pipe_table_row` sites over 14 of 738 corpus files produce no symbols, and the header-only reading is what the M11 contract named when it fixed the lane's symbol map (`pipe_table -> class`, columns as `contains` children).
decisions.consequence: A table's data is not queryable through this lane. For a documentation graph that is the right trade — the structure is the document's, the values are the reader's — and it is the same ruling toml's spec records for a value being data rather than a node.
decisions.pinned_by: the M12 contract probe's 'contains table -> column', and markdown/payload-lines-evidence for the column edges' line and tier.

decisions.question: Should a raw HTML block publish a symbol? RULED: no, and the cost is attributed to the GRAMMAR rather than the analyzer.
decisions.measured: 579 `html_block` sites over 291 of 738 corpus files. The corpus-errors artifact already names the one construct where the block grammar genuinely fails rather than declining: an indented `<details>` inside a numbered-list item, which recovers with an ERROR node at each list-item boundary, in 2 of 738 files. The remaining 577 sites are regions the grammar models as opaque and the lane correctly declines to invent structure for.
decisions.consequence: A document that is largely HTML (a generated API reference, say) contributes only its markdown skeleton to the graph. Declared, not hidden — and the alternative, fabricating a tree for a region the parser did not resolve, is the 'a guess dressed as a fact' the erlang/html lanes both record as a refusal.
decisions.pinned_by: validation/m12/results/markdown-corpus-errors.json, whose four named grammar limits are the measured half of this ruling.

decisions.question: The block grammar wraps content in `section` nodes. Should a `section` be a symbol, or should the heading hierarchy BE the containment tree? RULED: the heading hierarchy is the tree, and `section` is an internal artifact.
decisions.measured: The M11 contract fixed the symbol map as 'ATX headings -> type with hierarchy', and the M12 ground truth's 59 facts are all heading/table/code containment with no `section` among them.
decisions.consequence: A heading is the document's own structure and a `section` is the grammar's, so publishing the latter would put a node in the graph that no author wrote and no reader navigates by. The heading hierarchy carries the same information with a name the document chose.
decisions.pinned_by: the 59 M12 ground-truth facts and the 31-check M12 contract probe, both of which would gain a `section` row if this ruling were reversed.

_sectionsBEH.note: Sections B-H are not carried in this file. B (every relationship kind pinned) and C (the payload matrix) are declared in script/m14/completeness-inventory.ts's LANG_CONFIGS entry, D (>=2 distinct evidenceClass pinned) and E/F (the differential floor and the perf budget) are read from the F3 fixtures and the differential baseline, G from the two docs, and H from M14.CC1.json. markdown is NOT in GATED_LANGS and the ladder is the reason: a language joins when all eight sections are green, and G is not satisfiable yet because docs/analyzers/markdown.md does not exist (M14 section G requires BOTH the <lang>.md and the real-<lang>-analyzer.md doc), and E is not satisfiable from a scoped run because the canonical M14.0.F5.json belongs to the 34-language sweep. Both are named as owed rather than worked around.

relationship_kinds_declared_absent.imports: markdown has no module system. There is nothing to import, and a `uses` edge to a relative path is a LINK, not a dependency — bb_doc's Dependencies section stays empty for a .md file for exactly this reason, which is a real consequence of the ruling and not an oversight.
relationship_kinds_declared_absent.exports: a markdown file exports nothing; it is a leaf of the project's file tree.
relationship_kinds_declared_absent.calls: no call syntax exists in CommonMark.
relationship_kinds_declared_absent.extends: no inheritance syntax exists in CommonMark.
relationship_kinds_declared_absent.implements: no interface syntax exists in CommonMark.
relationship_kinds_declared_absent.overrides: no member syntax exists in CommonMark.
relationship_kinds_declared_absent.instantiates: no constructor syntax exists in CommonMark.
relationship_kinds_declared_absent.references: the lane declares front-matter keys as a boundary rather than a graph: `title:`, `permalink:`, `redirect_from:` and `weight:` are the cross-file link carriers in a Jekyll site and the block grammar models `minus_metadata` as ONE node with no key/value children, so there is no key to reference from. Declared, with the reason, rather than left silent.

payload_fields_pinned.range: markdown/payload-lines-evidence — every symbol carries a 1-based startLine/endLine, and the store's (file, name, startLine) key is what makes two sites of one construct distinct rows.
payload_fields_pinned.visibility: every markdown symbol is `public`; there is no private or package scope in a document, so the field is constant rather than absent.
payload_fields_pinned.ownerName: markdown/code-block-site-identity and heading-identity pin owner attribution, including the case that broke it (a repeated heading's children must attach to the right occurrence).
payload_fields_pinned.metadata: markdown/code-block-site-identity pins nodeType/language/isMarkdownCodeBlock/isRepeatedSite at the ANALYZER seam. NOT pinned at the WORKER seam, and the reason is recorded there: pool-worker's BasicSymbol projection narrows symbol.metadata to a 15-key CSS-only allowlist, and the F3 lane calls engine.parseFile rather than the worker, so no fixture can currently see the difference. Named as owed rather than claimed.

evidence_tiers.contains: structural — a parent/child relation read off the block tree
evidence_tiers.uses: reference_qualified — the destination is a node's own text, and for a reference link the destination the document's own definition declares
evidence_tiers.measured: 11,401/11,401 relationships over the pinned corpus carry a 1-based line_number and an evidenceClass from the closed vocabulary. Before this round it was 0/9,132, and because graph-core's read-time derivation does not list `contains` among its structural types the entire heading hierarchy was rendered to readers as `inferred` — 'a guess, treat as a hint, never as fact' — for edges that cannot be anything else.
